🔥 बॉलीवुड में अपनी फिटनेस और ट्रांसफॉर्मेशन को लेकर श्रियम् भगनानी ने खोले कई दिलचस्प राज! 😱

1️⃣ श्रियम् भगनानी ने स्पोर्ट्स बायोपिक फिल्म Sumo Didi से अपना लीड रोल डेब्यू किया है, जो भारत की इकलौती महिला सूमो रेसलर हेतल दवे की जिंदगी से प्रेरित है। 🤼‍♀️
2️⃣ एक्ट्रेस का कहना है कि उनका ऑडिशन बिल्कुल अलग था जिसमें उन्हें मैदान पर दौड़ने, वर्कआउट करने और फिर फिल्म का एक मिरर सीन करने को कहा गया था। 🏃‍♀️
3️⃣ प्रोड्यूसर के दावे के मुताबिक, उस समय तीन लड़कियों को चुना गया था और तीनों को ट्रेनिंग दी गई थी ताकि यह देखा जा सके कि कौन शारीरिक डिमांड संभाल सकता है, और श्रियम् को इसकी भनक बाद में लगी। 🤫
4️⃣ तैयारी के बारे में श्रियम् ने बताया कि उन्होंने हर दिन 8 से 9 घंटे ट्रेनिंग की, जिसमें जिम ट्रेनर, फिजियोथैरेपिस्ट, योगा ट्रेनर और हेतल दवे के साथ सूमो ट्रेनिंग शामिल थी और यह सब लगभग नौ महीने तक चला। 💪
5️⃣ श्रियम् के मुताबिक, उन्हें पहले एक बड़े बैनर की फिल्म के लिए 30 किलो वजन घटाने को कहा गया था लेकिन फिल्म बंद हो गई, और एक अन्य प्रोजेक्ट में डायरेक्टर नागेश कुकुनूर के कहने पर 10 किलो वजन बढ़ाया था, लेकिन बाद में प्रोजेक्ट से हटा दिया गया। 📉

क्या आप भी श्रियम् भगनानी की यह फिल्म देखने के लिए एक्साइटेड हैं? नीचे कमेंट्स में बताओ! 👇✨

ctx.title: Exclusive! Shriyam Bhagnani On Unconventional Audition For Sumo Didi: “3 Of Us Underwent Training Before Being Finalized”
ctx.summary:
Shriyam Bhagnani made her debut as solo lead in the recently released ZEE5 film, Sumo Didi. She speaks to Koimoi about her experience of landing the film after multiple rejections and drastic transformations.  
 The post  Exclusive! Shriyam Bhagnani On Unconventional Audition For Sumo Didi: “3 Of Us Underwent Training Before Being Finalized”  appeared first on  Koimoi .
ctx.text:
Shriyam Bhagnani made her lead debut with a rather unconventional biopic titled Sumo Didi. The film is inspired by the life of India’s only female sumo wrestler, Hetal Dave. The actress speaks to us about the untold stories behind the film’s making.
After years of unexpected turns, abandoned projects, and demanding physical preparation, Shriyam Bhagnani found a role that required her to embrace a transformation unlike any other. The actress opens up about her journey with Sumo Didi, the nine-month training process, and why she stays away from misleading advertisements.
The actress, who made her lead-role debut in the sports biopic, had to undergo a significant physical transformation to play her character. But the road to the film was not as straightforward as it might seem. There were projects that fell through, demanding weight changes and moments when she had to trust that things would eventually work out.
The actress sat down with Koimoi for a heartfelt conversation about her journey to be part of the film.
Before landing the role, she had to prove that she was physically fit for the part. The makers had noticed her work in City of Dreams, following which she was called in for an audition. The audition itself was unlike a conventional screen test. “For the audition, I was asked to run around on the ground, do some workouts. They probably wanted to see the athleticism in everyone. That went on, and then we were made to wait for 15-20 minutes. Then we did this mirror scene in the film as the audition,” she said after which she was selected.
However, Shriyam later learned that she was not the only one selected. “Much later, the producer said that three girls were selected at that time. All three of us were put into training. And they checked who was capable of the training. They chose me, and I had no idea about this till much later.”
She later learned that three actresses had initially been selected and put through training, with the team assessing who could handle the role’s physical demands. Shriyam, however, had no idea that she was part of this process until much later.
Playing a sumo wrestler required more than simply looking the part. Having been away from sports for nearly a decade, Shriyam had to retrain herself from scratch. The preparation involved an entire team of professionals, including a gym trainer, a physiotherapist, and a yoga trainer, as well as specialized sumo training under Hetal Dave.
“It was eight to nine hours of training every day. And then there were script readings in between. I had to move out of my house to another area because I couldn’t come back home after all this. The training lasted for almost nine months,” she says.
Hetal Dave, who trained her in judo and sumo wrestling, was closely involved throughout the process. “Every single day, we would meet and train. I would cry after going home because it used to hurt a lot,” she recalled. The effort eventually paid off. When Hetal watched the film for the first time alongside Shriyam, she was moved to tears and particularly happy with how her family dynamics were portrayed.
The film also gave Shriyam an opportunity to understand the cultural significance of sumo wrestling in Japan. During the shoot, the team filmed at a sumo temple, where the sport’s practice is treated as a ritual. She also interacted with international sumo wrestlers who appear in the film.
“I learned that sumo wrestlers are genuinely superstars in Japan. They are really respected. I also learned that they are very healthy. My first shock was that I thought I would have to gain weight, but you actually have to put on a lot of muscle. It’s healthy weight gain,” she explains.
While gaining weight for Sumo Didi was part of the role, it was not the first time Shriyam had been asked to undergo a drastic physical transformation for a project. In fact, two earlier experiences had already shaped her relationship with such demands.
